comments.text:
This layoff incident appears to be a strategic plot by MS, Sam, and Ilya, deliberately aimed at dismantling OpenAI. Originally established as a non-profit, OpenAI filled its board with individuals unconnected to its core mission, which led to constraints as the organization shifted towards profit-making activities. Over time, OpenAI's non-profit status became a limitation, prompting its disassembly. Ilya, in a calculated move, took on the role of the antagonist, championing the safe development of AGI under the pretense of altruism. He likely anticipated this development, and amidst the unfolding reality that all OpenAI staff would be integrated into MS, the latter is seemingly receptive.

Holding a 49% stake without any representation on the board or a voice in decision-making is nonsensical for MS. While there are considerable growth prospects ahead, OpenAI’s non-profit nature is a stumbling block. There's reasonable suspicion that MS, alongside Altman and Ilya, orchestrated the breakup of OpenAI. Given Ilya's position as a co-founder and major contributor to GPT, he possesses the authority to stress the importance of AGI, making him a suitable figurehead for this act. Moreover, it’s common knowledge that many OpenAI employees have shares in the company, and with the organization's valuation predicted to fall, their overt backing of Sam Altman follows logically. The notion that they or Ilya himself were oblivious to the eventual outcome of these events is highly unlikely.

comments.author: @gregorykennedy-mindfuldude
comments.text:
Nobody right, Nobody wrong.  Thanks Wes for your always excellent content.  I am a former SC Valley corp engineer.  I had seen this letter earlier and find it a bit suspect, especially now that it has been taken down.  Looking at things from several perspectives.  

There could have been turmoil during the 2016 OpenAI transition period for sure.  We should all be reminded that OpenAI was originally supposed to be Open Source and that is what was so exciting and interesting about OpenAi from the beginning.  

Then there was the fallout with Elon and the others and Elon left.  OpenAI switched to a hybrid non-profit, for profit and I am sure this ruffled the feathers of those who joined the company passionate about creating the worlds best Open source models.  

However the other side is that Sams understanding that it would take lots of cash and massive compute power to build something remarkable (something worth remarking about) is and was not wrong obviously as all of us have witnessed the result.  GPT4 is incredible and the release of GPT 3.5 was the spark that ignited the llm fire as numerous other Open source, semi-open and closed source models have been released arguably due to OpenAI's move fast and break things approach.

The OpenAI board seemed to live up to their stated goals and responsibility (although the board member from Quora/Poe should have probably resigned from the board for conflict of interest reasons) and clearly handled their non-profit/for proit conflict with Sam and Greg unprofessionally.

In the end I believe that there is Nobody right and Nobody wrong in this PR debacle and that this very public shakeup has taught and is teaching the world a lesson in non-profit and corporate governance structure, and alignment of team members and goals, while also allowing the space for serious critique and discusion.  Thanks again Wes as I have been following your excellent take and overview of the situation.

comments.text:
It's ancient, and sounds kinda meh. I'm sure the culture really was different back in 2018, and before they had found much success.

It's also true that Sam Altman strikes me as a somewhat mousy guy. But... You usually need some character flaws driving you. The most mature seeming people are usually, not as successful. And I do think that he's broadly well intentioned.

Most of the complaints just sound like crap that you find at many a young and immature company. Perhaps especially ones that aren't successful and don't have an obvious path to success yet, while they're burning money... If in that state, you don't trust each other yet... It is what it is.

As for the *censored* case... We do all have our own instincts and biases. It's no easy thing to accept someone your programming isn't inclined to accept.

Like, personally, I judge people off of my intuitive sense of their character... Which is usually correct. But, even if it is quite often correct... How far can you trust an evolved algorithm?

It is, somewhat unfair, to not give talented people a chance, due to things outside of their control... Witness the case of Alan Turing.

Anyway, I'm not sure complaints from 2018 and whatever state OpenAI was in at the time, really pertain to the situation now... And we know enough about how the board blundered into firing Sam. And it was not for any of these reasons. At most, Sam was probably too motivated to build cool things and make the right decisions for the company (from a product standpoint).

The board reacted badly, in part due to imagined risk (not on the AI side exactly), and perhaps because of the undisclosed conflict of interest that D'Angelo had... As we can generally see from OpenAI's employees... Sam does have their trust as a leader. They don't think he's replaceable.

comments.text:
To begin, Elon appears somewhat foolish, though he does have some commendable ideas. A prime illustration is his recent AI venture, which seems reminiscent of edgy 2007 4chan nonsense. It's advisable to take Elon's statements with a small dose of scepticism. While investigating the authenticity of the letter you should investigate Elon's actual involvement, we should be cautious not to overlook the possibility that Elon orchestrated this letter, presenting a seemingly random email as evidence the company is `falling apart` but we may also find that some of this could be the reason Elon left and he just wanted to get it off his chest without breaching some sort of NDA by presenting it as a `random email`. Additionally, Microsoft wouldn't maintain such close ties with Sam if there were any truth to the rumours. The CEO of Microsoft has demonstrated genuine character, and it's unlikely he would lavish Sam with benefits if he believed the speculations were valid. His actions suggest that he has encountered information contradicting the falsehoods and propaganda surrounding the situation at openai but wants to keep the peace between both Sam and OAI. Elon needs to go back to sorting `X¬Twitter` the sausage.

(I actually just read other comments which suggest the same as me, Elon wrote this himself.)

PS: Brock's comment might hold some truth, given my understanding of software engineers. They typically possess a broad perspective on life and often avoid delving deeply into gender-related issues. While I'm not defending Brock, it's worth considering that his words may not have been intended to directly offend anyone. The amplification of the situation, fuelled by the current "woke" culture and cancel culture, turned it into a more significant issue than it originally was. This led to Brock deciding not to engage with the person further, causing the individual to feel targeted. While I can't assert this with certainty, many would acknowledge that such dynamics are common in workplaces. It's often the person taking offense who contributes to creating a hostile work environment. It's important to recognize that programmers and software engineers tend to be introspective, spending the majority of their time in their own thoughts, socializing infrequently, and paying minimal attention to external affairs. It's simply looked at "be who you want to be, but don't impose it on others" types of situations and before someone chimes. I understand people are different this is just an example. It's very grey area to walk across when it comes to gender subjects.

Here is the letter:
11/21/2023
To the Board of Directors of OpenAI:
We are writing to you today to express our deep concern about the recent events at OpenAI, particularly the allegations of misconduct against Sam Altman.
We are former OpenAI employees who left the company during a period of significant turmoil and upheaval. As you have now witnessed what happens when you dare stand up to Sam Altman, perhaps you can understand why so many of us have remained silent for fear of repercussions. We can no longer stand by silent.
We believe that the Board of Directors has a duty to investigate these allegations thoroughly and take appropriate action. We urge you to:
	•	Expand the scope of Emmett’s investigation to include an examination of Sam Altman’s actions since August 2018, when OpenAI began transitioning from a non-profit to a for-profit entity.
	•	Issue an open call for private statements from former OpenAI employees who resigned, were placed on medical leave, or were terminated during this period.
	•	Protect the identities of those who come forward to ensure that they are not subjected to retaliation or other forms of harm.
We believe that a significant number of OpenAI employees were pushed out of the company to facilitate its transition to a for-profit model. This is evidenced by the fact that OpenAI’s employee attrition rate between January 2018 and July 2020 was in the order of 50%.
Throughout our time at OpenAI, we witnessed a disturbing pattern of deceit and manipulation by Sam Altman and Greg Brockman, driven by their insatiable pursuit of achieving artificial general intelligence (AGI). Their methods, however, have raised serious doubts about their true intentions and the extent to which they genuinely prioritize the benefit of all humanity.
Many of us, initially hopeful about OpenAI’s mission, chose to give Sam and Greg the benefit of the doubt. However, as their actions became increasingly concerning, those who dared to voice their concerns were silenced or pushed out. This systematic silencing of dissent created an environment of fear and intimidation, effectively stifling any meaningful discussion about the ethical implications of OpenAI’s work.
We provide concrete examples of Sam and Greg’s dishonesty & manipulation including:
	•	Sam’s demand for researchers to delay reporting progress on specific “secret” research initiatives, which were later dismantled for failing to deliver sufficient results quickly enough. Those who questioned this practice were dismissed as “bad culture fits” and even terminated, some just before Thanksgiving 2019.
	•	Greg’s use of discriminatory language against a gender-transitioning team member. Despite many promises to address this issue, no meaningful action was taken, except for Greg simply avoiding all communication with the affected individual, effectively creating a hostile work environment. This team member was eventually terminated for alleged under-performance.
	•	Sam directing IT and Operations staff to conduct investigations into employees, including Ilya, without the knowledge or consent of management.
	•	Sam’s discreet, yet routine exploitation of OpenAI’s non-profit resources to advance his personal goals, particularly motivated by his grudge against Elon following their falling out.
	•	The Operations team’s tacit acceptance of the special rules that applied to Greg, navigating intricate requirements to avoid being blacklisted.
	•	Brad Lightcap’s unfulfilled promise to make public the documents detailing OpenAI’s capped-profit structure and the profit cap for each investor.
	•	Sam’s incongruent promises to research projects for compute quotas, causing internal distrust and infighting.
Despite the mounting evidence of Sam and Greg’s transgressions, those who remain at OpenAI continue to blindly follow their leadership, even at significant personal cost. This unwavering loyalty stems from a combination of fear of retribution and the allure of potential financial gains through OpenAI’s profit participation units.
The governance structure of OpenAI, specifically designed by Sam and Greg, deliberately isolates employees from overseeing the for-profit operations, precisely due to their inherent conflicts of interest. This opaque structure enables Sam and Greg to operate with impunity, shielded from accountability.
We urge the Board of Directors of OpenAI to take a firm stand against these unethical practices and launch an independent investigation into Sam and Greg’s conduct. We believe that OpenAI’s mission is too important to be compromised by the personal agendas of a few individuals.
We implore you, the Board of Directors, to remain steadfast in your commitment to OpenAI’s original mission and not succumb to the pressures of profit-driven interests. The future of artificial intelligence and the well-being of humanity depend on your unwavering commitment to ethical leadership and transparency.
Sincerely,
Concerned Former OpenAI Employees
Contact
We encourage former OpenAI employees to contact us at formerly_openai@mail2tor.com. We personally guarantee everyone’s anonymity in any internal deliberations and public communications.
Further Updates
Updates will be posted at https://board.net/p/r.e6a8f6578787a4cc67d4dc438c6d236e
